newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab League demands Turkey withdraw from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Arab League demands Turkey withdraw from Iraq.

text.p: The Arab League secretariat on Monday condemned Turkey's military operations in northern Iraq and demanded Turkish forces withdraw immediately.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the region to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
Iraq says it has complained to the U.N. Security Council about the Turkish attacks but its pleas have gone unanswered.

The secretariat of the Cairo-based league said in a statement: "(We) are following with grave concern the latest developments arising from the large-scale and continuing Turkish invasion deep into Iraqi territory."
"The continuation of this aggression is likely to have a negative effect on the historical ties of friendship and cooperation between the Arab states and Turkey," it added.

"The secretariat...strongly condemns the Turkish military invasion of Iraqi territory and demands that Turkey withdraw its military forces immediately...and refrain from repeating these violations of the sovereignty of Iraq.

"The exceptional situation in northern Iraq must not be exploited and any security or other measures, under any pretext, likely to affect the sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq and its territorial integrity are unacceptable," it said.
Turkey says that the aim of the operations is only to eliminate PKK bases inside Iraq and that it has no designs on Iraqi territory or hostility towards the Baghdad government.
